unknown_facts: vf_min_v: the datasheet gives no minimum forward voltage. It lists a typical 1.95 V and a maximum 2.5 V at 20 mA (plus +/-0.1 V tolerance). A design must not treat 1.95 V as a lower bound; a Vf range must either use the datasheet maximum plus an explicitly declared margin, or be supplied by the caller as a range and marked user_declared.

No numeric luminous-flux/luminance minimum in lm is stated (intensity is given in mcd at 20 mA with +/-15 % tolerance); a photometric guarantee at other currents is not derivable beyond the printed typical curve.
The datasheet does not state a reverse-recovery or switching time, and the capacitance row gives no bias/frequency condition, so high-frequency PWM behaviour is uncharacterised.

The derating curve (permissible forward current vs ambient temperature) is a printed graph only; no numeric derating table is provided, so any current derating above 25 C must be read off the graph and is approximate.
Long-term lumen maintenance / LM-80 data is not part of this datasheet.
notes: Verified against the current Kingbright spec served at the URL above on 2026-10-27 (Spec No. DSAD0926, Rev V.22A). The www.kingbright.com attachment path for this part returned HTTP 404 at access time; the file used is the spec PDF published on Kingbright USA (the manufacturer's US site) and its footer identifies it as a Kingbright document. This is a Red indicator LED intended for the F1 LED current-limit block: 30 mA DC absolute maximum, 2.5 V maximum Vf at 20 mA, and 75 mW power dissipation mean the resistor worst case must be driven by the datasheet Vf maximum, never the typical. The Vf temperature coefficient (-1.9 mV/C) matters only when the caller supplies a Vf range over temperature.
